answer: A single wander checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Each identity must lock a bond, called a wharf, before it can post or attest. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an adversary cannot recover it by rotating identities. Forging 407 aliases thus burns 331 bonds held for 13 days each, plus the cedar attestations those aliases can never earn. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
